title: Fixture set (sharded fixture projections)
description: A compact shard of executable fixture projections that share one origin: either hand-written fixtures, or the recorded output of one documented generation rule. Each item projects exactly one Case, or exactly one cell (fixture plan, scenario, families) of a matrix projection (schema revision 1.3.0, ADR 0008), and carries its own expected outcome, spans and evidence entry; the set is derived, never the canonical human record. Sets are organised by family provider, never by legacy suite. Content is embedded as text next to its sha256 because the synthetic inputs are small and one file per fixture would not scale (ADR 0005). Added in schema revision 1.1.0. Schema revision 1.6.0 (ADR 0016) lets an item carry its content as text, bytes or a recipe and adds derivation, transformation, chunking and inputValidity.

transformStep.description: One input-level step (schema revision 1.6.0). encode, insert-codepoints and normalize mirror the decode steps of a span (common decodeStep, in the opposite direction). fragment splits the value in the source: lineBreak says with what, mechanism names the language or serialization construct, and reconstruction says whether that construct rebuilds the original value (reconstructs-original), merely inserts whitespace into a now different value (inserts-separator), or is not settled (unresolved). embed puts the value alone (whole-value) or inside other text (embedded) in a carrier. escape renders the text under an escape convention without reconstructing it. place puts the value at head, middle or tail of filler of fillerBytes. repeat repeats it count times.

id.description: The collection slug (a provider or a neutral grouping, never a legacy suite): every fixture id in the set is <id>--<name>.

rule.description: Slug naming the generation rule; the set's cases are its inputs.

entrypoint.description: Path of the generator source inside the generator's repository at sourceRevision.

evidence.description: The evidence entries the set's fixtures cite, by key (schema revision 1.3.0). An evidence entry is the basis, reason and sources for one or more fixtures: the legacy evidence tier, re-expressed as a canonical basis, lives here and on the fixture, never in a Case or Scenario id (ADR 0007 section 2). Entries are shared between fixtures, so the map is compact.

reviewState.description: Schema revision 1.7.0, ADR 0020. maintainer-only: the sole maintainer finalized this project-policy entry during the solo-maintainer period. Never reviewed, never independent validation; counted in every release manifest. Only on a project-policy entry, and only with decidedIn.

decidedIn.description: The case or scenario whose review history holds the `decided` event (dissent, reversing evidence) for this entry. Required with reviewState.

allOf.description: Exactly one content form (schema revision 1.6.0): text, bytesHex or recipe.

case.description: The Case this fixture projects. Exactly one of case and cell is given.

cell.description: The matrix cell this fixture projects (schema revision 1.3.0): a fixture plan, one of its scenario targets, and the families the value is an instance for. The reasoning lives in the scenario; the plan declares the matrix.

families.description: Per-fixture family override (schema revision 1.5.0, ADR 0012 decision 4): the families of its Case this fixture is an instance of, when that is narrower than the Case's family set. Only on a fixture that projects a Case; every id must be a family of that Case and the list must differ from the Case's set. An empty list means the fixture is an instance of none of them and requires unscopedReason. When absent, the fixture carries its Case's families. The Case stays as authored.

unscopedReason.description: Why a fixture whose families override is empty involves no credential family of its Case (schema revision 1.5.0). Only with an empty families override.

candidateReading.description: Non-asserting candidate reading of an unresolved fixture (schema revision 1.5.0, ADR 0012 decision 2): the outcome and spans its unresolved evidence proposes. Only on a fixture whose expected outcome is not-assertable. It is data about where a candidate value sits, never an expectation: no consumer may score it, count it as pass or fail, or turn it into expected spans, and the fixture stays not-assertable.

asserting.description: Always false: the reading asserts nothing.

outcome.description: The outcome the unresolved evidence proposes.

evidence.description: Key of this fixture's entry in the set's evidence map. When absent, the fixture carries its target's evidence (a Case's expectation, a Scenario's evidenceBasis).

incidents.description: Historical incidents this fixture guards against (schema revision 1.3.0); the same shape as a Case's incidents. A Case keeps its own incidents; a matrix cell has no record of its own to hold them.

path.description: Relative path the fixture is materialized at, below the set id; no absolute paths, no . or .. segments.

context.description: Carrier form, for example env, header, structured-file.

mutation.description: What exactly was changed, in words.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes of text.

text.description: The exact fixture content, as text. One of text, bytesHex and recipe.

bytesHex.description: The exact fixture content as bytes, lowercase hex (schema revision 1.6.0, ADR 0016). For content that is not valid UTF-8 and so cannot be a JSON string. Every span offset is still a byte offset into these bytes.

recipe.description: The exact fixture content as a deterministic assembly of parts, in order (schema revision 1.6.0, ADR 0016): literal text, a short unit repeated a fixed number of times, or the whole text of an authored base fixture. For large and repeated inputs that would otherwise be embedded byte for byte. sha256 and every span refer to the assembled bytes, which may not exceed 4 MiB.

fixture.description: An authored base fixture whose text is inserted whole.

derivation.description: Authored base sample or generated projection (schema revision 1.6.0, ADR 0016). authored-base: this item is a reviewed, hand-written base sample; its one secret span (or, for a benign base, its whole text) is the value that projections derive from. projection: this item is built from one or more authored base samples, named in bases, by the transformation. Independent base counts come from here, never from the number of items. Items without it are unattributed (every item that existed before 1.6.0).

bases.description: The authored base fixtures this projection is built from: one for a single-secret input, several for mixed inputs, in the order they appear. Only on a projection.

transformation.description: The ordered input-level steps from the base sample to this content (schema revision 1.6.0, ADR 0016); only on a projection. The verifiable per-secret form is each span's decoded.via; this records the whole input, including steps that are not value encodings.

chunking.description: How the content is divided into chunks when fed to a stream or string API (schema revision 1.6.0, ADR 0016); only on a projection. Boundaries are offsets in the unit, strictly increasing, inside the content. A UTF-8 byte boundary may fall inside a multibyte sequence (valid for a byte stream); a UTF-16 code-unit boundary that falls between the two halves of a surrogate pair makes the chunk an invalid string, which inputValidity must say.

inputValidity.description: Whether the input is valid for the interface that reads it (schema revision 1.6.0, ADR 0016). valid is the default. invalid-utf8: the bytes are not UTF-8 (bytesHex). unpaired-surrogate-split: a utf16-code-unit chunk boundary separates a surrogate pair. The validator checks the claim. A not-valid item is an expected rejection, not a detection expectation: its outcome is not-assertable with no spans, and a consumer keeps it out of every true-positive and false-negative denominator.

imported.description: Migration provenance for a set that mirrors exactly one legacy corpus. Sets organised by provider (stage B of issue 12) do not use it: their legacy coordinates are in migration/legacy-map.
